title: Exhaustive documentation audit and drift removal
description:
The documentation-accuracy epic (287c4051) corrected verified drift and installed the `doc-review` gate. That gate audits by sampling and descends into fresh territory each pass; over ten rounds it surfaced 59 real defects, and much of the adopter surface (`how-to/`, most of `examples/`, `tutorials/`) was never sampled. This epic guarantees completeness: an exhaustive, source-verified pass over the entire adopter-facing documentation surface so no stale claim survives, plus structural prevention for the highest-risk facts.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every factual claim about CLI behavior, storage layout, repository structure, and engine semantics in the in-scope surface is verified against the current source tree; none contradicts source.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every documented command and flag matches `jit --schema`; every source-path/code citation resolves to a real file; every internal link and heading anchor resolves.
- [hard] REQ-03: Shipped docs state current behavior only — no legacy or future/roadmap narration.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every diagram in the in-scope surface is a Mermaid block; no ASCII or arrow-art diagrams, including unicode-arrow spines.
- [hard] REQ-05: Every top-level `jit` command family present in `jit --schema` has an adopter-facing documentation home.
- [hard] REQ-06: Volatile facts (enums, CLI shapes, invariant/rule/gate text, storage specifics) are projected or cited (`@/inv`, `@/rule`, `@/gate`, `jit --schema`, `jit invariant render`, `jit reference render`) rather than hand-copied, wherever an existing projection or citation surface covers the fact (`@/inv/single-source-prose`).

## In-scope surface

`docs/` (concepts, reference, how-to, tutorials, examples) plus root `README.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `TESTING.md`, `mcp-server/README.md`, `web/README.md`.

## Planning constraints (bind the plan; do not relitigate)

- **Decomposition axis** — by doc area, five broad areas, each with a disjoint file footprint: (1) `concepts/`, (2) `reference/`, (3) `how-to/` + `tutorials/`, (4) `examples/` (all seven rulesets), (5) root + `mcp-server/README.md` + `web/README.md`.
- **Per-area acceptance bar** (this is what makes it exhaustive rather than sampled): every documented command/flag checked against `jit --schema`; every source citation resolves to a real file; every internal link and anchor resolves; every diagram is Mermaid; then `doc-review` passes on the area.
- **Gap-filling (REQ-05)** — cover only top-level `jit` command families absent from the docs entirely. Individual flag-level gaps are handled by the corrective pass, not treated as new-doc mandates.
- **Structural prevention (REQ-06)** — citations and existing projection surfaces only. No new `jit`/engine features. Where a volatile fact has no projection surface today, cite the source file and file a follow-up for the projection rather than building it inside this epic.
- **Deletion / merge policy** — a task may delete a wholly-obsolete or redundant doc, or merge it into another, repointing inbound links, with the rationale recorded on the task.
- **Examples** — audit all seven rulesets, but first triage reference-grade (full source verification) versus illustrative (lighter consistency pass); record the triage and let depth follow it.
- **Style** — factual accuracy only; punctuation/tone rewrites are not an acceptance criterion (cf. 287c4051 LD-11).

## Non-goals

- No changes to `dev/` contributor docs or `CLAUDE.md`.

## Drift evidence

Seven recurring drift classes are catalogued in the linked planning brief and in `dev/archive/287c4051-completion-report.md` (Holistic Quality Notes): (1) `.jit/` described as all state, (2) atomic `rename()` over-credited versus advisory locks, (3) storage-format specifics (ID scheme, state enum, event shape, gate-runs layout), (4) future/roadmap narration, (5) legacy narration of current surface, (6) nonexistent CLI surface, (7) prerequisite/environment drift.
